claims.title: Propose one actor boundary with explicit fallback policy
claims.why_now: Persistence and notification consumers derive different actors from the same context shape. For actorId=41, assignment self-notification suppression receives null while persistence receives 41. This is a source-supported architectural proposal; canonical precedence and fallback still require agreement.

implementations.responsibility: Persistence attribution and realtime side-effect actor extraction
Assignment actor extraction used to suppress self-notifications
Existing positive-ID normalization and explicit-context actor boundary

comparisons.input_case: Only actorId=41 is supplied; no user or ambient authentication

outcomes.behavior: Returns 41 from the explicit actorId branch
Returns null because context.user is absent

comparisons.input_case: actorId=0 and context.user.id=73; no ambient authentication

outcomes.behavior: Returns 73 from user.id; actorId is ignored
Returns null because an explicit non-null actorId takes precedence and fails positivity
Falls through to user.id and returns 73
Returns null; invalid explicit actorId does not fall through to user

comparisons.input_case: Context is empty and ambient Auth::id() would return 73

outcomes.behavior: Returns null; the helper does not read ambient authentication

comparisons.input_case: Only context.user.id=73 is supplied, with no getId method
Only context.user with getId()=73 and no public id is supplied; no ambient authentication

outcomes.behavior: Returns null after the property check and absent ambient authentication
Returns null because user.id is absent

consumer_changes.change: Replace the private resolver calls at persistence attribution and realtime side-effect sites with ActorContext::id after approving precedence. If persistence must preserve ambient fallback, materialize that actor into the context once at the request/transaction boundary; do not add hidden authentication to the shared helper.

Use ActorContext::id in handleCreate and handleAssignmentChange, then retire the duplicate private resolver. Preserve skip/support/positive-assignee checks and compare the canonical actor with the assigned user before sending.

Retain this existing owner. Decide whether invalid explicit IDs stop resolution or fall through, whether getId takes precedence over the public property, and whether numeric fractional strings are acceptable before migrating callers.

preserved_behavior: Self-assignment suppresses notification when the canonical actor equals the assigned user
Actor context remains tenant/request-bound and nullable for actorless jobs
Persistence, audit and realtime effects use the same approved actor for one operation
No shared helper starts reading ambient auth as an incidental side effect
missing_evidence: No repository-approved precedence/invalid-ID/ambient-fallback contract was supplied; ActorContext is a proposed survivor, not an approved replacement
Captured zero callers for ActorContext do not prove whole-application unreachability; analysis coverage and candidate search are incomplete
verification_steps: After contract approval, execute the six listed input cases for every migrated consumer, including worker and authenticated-request contexts
Verify create/update attribution, audit/realtime payloads and assignment notification suppression preserve the approved actor
Verify invalid, fractional and negative numeric inputs and objects with divergent getId/id values; no runtime check was executed in this review

claims.title: Separate evidence file handling from evidence acceptance rules
claims.why_now: The same class both applies requirement/exclusion/context decisions and reads/writes JSON artifacts. These responsibilities change for different reasons. This is a proposed split based on captured method behavior, not class length or method names alone.

implementations.responsibility: Evidence requirement decisions and artifact transport currently share one owner

consumer_changes.change: Keep the existing public service as the domain-facing facade; isolate report/template emission, directory checks and manifest decoding behind a narrow artifact owner. Reuse the existing framework File and JSON facilities, and preserve the existing profile/input-normalization collaborators instead of adding parallel resolvers.

preserved_behavior: Keep explicit unsupported-exclusion and template-context validation
Preserve JSON decoding errors and the distinction between missing, malformed and valid evidence
Keep tenant-specific directories, manifest/report field shapes and reportPath/templatePath results
Preserve existing public CLI-facing service methods during extraction
missing_evidence: No existing project-local artifact owner with matching contracts has been established; select one before introducing a new class
The bounded profile does not cover every method, and no CLI or file-emission acceptance check was executed
verification_steps: Review existing artifact helpers before selecting the extraction target
Compare valid, missing and malformed manifests; tenant isolation; directory failures; JSON errors; and report/template return shapes
Keep CLI callers on the existing facade during extraction and execute their acceptance checks once CI resumes
